tokyo.why_pick: The Ginza subway line runs right through Nihombashi and Kyobashi to Asakusa, Ueno, Ginza, Omotesando and Shibuya with no changes, so every day on the plan is one train or a short flat walk. The Marunouchi lights are a 10-minute walk, and on 24 Dec the Hokuriku shinkansen leaves from Tokyo Station, 5–12 minutes away on foot. It is also calmer and a little cheaper than Ginza itself.

areas.to_the_plans: Marunouchi lights 10 min walk; Ginza 10–15 min walk or 1 stop; Tsukiji outer market 10 min by taxi; Asakusa 15–20 min and Ueno about 10 min on the Ginza line; Omotesando/Shibuya about 20–25 min on the Ginza line; Tokyo Station 5–12 min walk; Haneda about 30 min by van.

St. Luke's International Hospital (obstetrics, 24-hour emergency) is about 5–10 min by taxi

areas.name: Ueno

good_for_us: Museums and Ueno Park on the doorstep for 22 Dec

The Hokuriku shinkansen to Nagano stops at Ueno
watch_out: Far from Tsukiji, Ginza and the Marunouchi lights

Furthest of the three from Haneda (about 40–50 min by van)

areas.station: Ueno (JR, Ginza and Hibiya lines), 3–10 min

tips: On 23 Dec the hotel front desk can send the big cases to Kyoto. Ask them to set the delivery for 30 Dec, and make sure someone at the Kyoto place can receive them. A self-check-in house may not be able to.
Ask for rooms on a high floor near the lift, and check that the hotel has twin or double beds for every couple plus a single for Tatiana. Tokyo rooms are small, so look at the square metres.
Check which subway exit has a lift (Kyobashi and Nihombashi both have some). Plan the Tsukiji and Haneda trips by taxi or van rather than by subway transfers.

The Hibiya line runs straight to Ueno for the late museum evening, and from Shinjuku on 7 Jan the Marunouchi line goes to Ginza with no change. Haneda is about 25–35 minutes by van on the Saturday, and the area will already feel familiar from 21 Dec.

Kabuki-za finishes late. A hotel within a 10-minute flat walk means Carlos, Nadir and Fernanda don't have to find a taxi.

yudanaka.why_pick: Only guests of Shibu inns get the key to the nine public baths, and the lantern lane is right outside the door, so staying here is what makes the plan work. Shibu is just 5 minutes by taxi from Yudanaka station and close to the monkey-park trailhead. Choose a modern inn with a lift, Western beds and rooms with their own bath. Some of the oldest wooden inns have steep stairs.

areas.to_the_plans: Monkey park 5 min to the trailhead plus a 30-min forest path; Shibu 5 min by car; Yudanaka station about 10 min by bus or taxi.
areas.station: Yudanaka (Nagaden), about 10 min by bus or taxi

tips: Ask each inn for: a room with Western beds, a lift (or a ground-floor room), and a private bath in the room or a private family bath you can book. Ask for an English menu for the Christmas Eve dinner. The best small inns fill up first for winter.
The monkey trail is a 30-minute forest walk, and it is often icy in December. Rent boot spikes at the trailhead. Fernanda should decide with her doctor. Winter cars can't reach the park.

Onsen are no longer officially off-limits in pregnancy (Japan dropped that warning in 2014), but avoid very hot water and long soaks. Shibu's public baths can be very hot, so the private bath is the safer choice.
The nearest hospital with obstetrics is Hokushin General Hospital in Nakano, about 15 min by taxi. Nagano Red Cross Hospital in Nagano city is a regional maternity centre, about 45–50 min away.

kanazawa.why_pick: Omicho and Musashi sit halfway between the station and the sights, on flat ground. It is 5 minutes by taxi to the station for the 8:40 Shirakawa-go bus, 10–15 minutes on foot to Higashi Chaya and 15–20 minutes to Kenroku-en and the 21st Century Museum. The market is right there for breakfast and for crab on the 28th, and the area has plenty of apartment-style rooms with washing machines.

tips: Book the Nohi bus to Shirakawa-go as soon as seats open, because reservations are required on most runs. Or book a private van for 7, which also means Fernanda doesn't have to stand around in the snow.
For an apartment, check: a washer (and ideally a dryer, since December is wet), the number of real beds, a lift, and heating in each room.

The nearest hospitals with obstetrics are Ishikawa Prefectural Central Hospital (north of the station) and Kanazawa University Hospital (east of Kenroku-en). Both are within 10–20 min by taxi of these areas.
Many Omicho shops close for the New Year holidays, but you leave on the 30th, so 29 Dec should be fine. Arrive early because it gets very busy.

kyoto.why_pick: The flat streets between the Kamo river and Yasaka Shrine are a 5–15 minute walk from the Okera fire, Nishiki market and Gion. Carlos, Nadir and Fernanda can walk home at 21:00 without taking a single step uphill. Keihan trains from Gion-Shijo run all night on New Year's Eve, and taxis can still reach this side, unlike the lanes up in Higashiyama, which are closed to cars from 21:00 on 31 Dec until 17:00 on 1 Jan.

Lots of atmosphere for a once-in-a-lifetime New Year

Taxis are very hard to get around midnight on 31 Dec
Feels far from Gion in the evenings
areas.to_the_plans: Yasaka 40 min walk or 15 min by taxi; Kyoto National Museum and Chishaku-in 20–25 min walk; Uji 17–30 min by JR; Nara 35–50 min by Kintetsu; shinkansen 5–10 min walk.

tips: Check the licence before you book any house. Kyoto lists licensed places, and a legal one shows a Hotel and Ryokan Act permit number or a home-sharing number starting with M26. A home-share in a residential-only zone may only take guests from mid-January to mid-March, so over New Year it would be illegal. Prefer a property with a full lodging permit.

Ask the machiya host: how many bedrooms are downstairs with real beds (Fernanda and Carlos and Nadir should be on the ground floor), how steep the stairs are, whether there's heating in every room (old houses are cold in January), whether there's a bath tub, and whether there's a washer.

Whole houses for 7 over New Year are among the first things to sell out in Kyoto, so book now. Kyoto's lodging tax rose in March 2026 and is charged per person, per night (¥200–¥10,000 depending on the price).

Chion-in's New Year's Eve bell needs a paid ticket booked in advance (it was ¥3,000 for 2025–26, with online sales from 1 Dec). Kodai-ji gives out numbered tickets from 22:00, and Eikando lets in whoever queues between 23:00 and 00:30.

kawaguchiko.why_pick: From the hotels on the east shore, across the big bridge from the station, rooms facing west look straight over the water to Fuji, which is perfect at dawn. They are still only about 5 minutes by taxi or hotel shuttle from the station and the ropeway. The Red Line sightseeing bus runs past to the Itchiku Kubota museum, so the group can manage without a car.

tips: Book a room type labelled 'Mt Fuji view' (or 'lake and Fuji view'), and ask for a high floor. Fuji is clearest in the early morning in January.
Ask for Western beds, and for an in-room or private bath. Many lake hotels have rooms with their own onsen bath, which suits Fernanda better than a shared bath.
There are three sightseeing bus lines: Red (east and north shores), Green (south shore to Lake Saiko) and Blue (Narusawa). They run only by day in winter, so plan on taxis after dark.
For hospitals, Yamanashi Red Cross (Funatsu) has an obstetrics clinic, but call to ask whether it handles births. Fujiyoshida Municipal Medical Center is 15–20 min by taxi.

Big hotels there have lifts and real beds. You get the old town by morning without a long walk with bags, which matters when the streets are icy in December and January.

East of the river, the Higashiyama side climbs uphill and is badly lit at night
areas.to_the_plans: Sanmachi 0–5 min; station 10–15 min walk or 5 min by taxi.

tips: Ask a ryokan for Western-bed rooms, a lift and an in-room bath. Many old-town inns use futons on tatami.
The New Year period is the exception to cheap winter rates, so book early. Snow lies on the ground from late December.
Takayama Red Cross Hospital in Tenmancho is the main hospital for the whole Hida region.

hakone.why_pick: Hakone-Yumoto is only 15 minutes from Odawara, where the shinkansen from Kyoto stops, and it is the closest part of Hakone to Odawara's maternity hospital. Many ryokan here offer beds and in-room baths, and taxis wait at the station. The Romancecar goes direct to Shinjuku when you leave. The higher villages (Miyanoshita, Gora) are steep, and Sengokuhara can only be reached by bus.

areas.name: Hakone-Yumoto
areas.what_its_like: The busy gateway hot-spring town along two rivers, full of ryokan, souvenir shops and places to eat.
good_for_us: Shortest trip from Odawara (15 min) with cabin bags
The most ryokan to choose from, at every price
Taxi rank at the station, restaurants and shops
Odawara Municipal Hospital (regional maternity centre) is about 20–25 min by taxi
Direct Romancecar to Shinjuku
watch_out: Busy with day-trippers
Some inns are across the river or up steep driveways, so pick one with a shuttle or take a taxi
Every sightseeing trip starts with the slow mountain train uphill
areas.to_the_plans: Odawara 15 min by train; Gora and the Open-Air Museum 35–40 min by mountain train; Lake Ashi 40 min by bus; Shinjuku about 85–90 min by Romancecar.
areas.station: Hakone-Yumoto (Odakyu / Hakone Tozan), 0–15 min walk or short taxi

areas.name: Miyanoshita
areas.what_its_like: A small, old-fashioned resort on the slope around the historic Fujiya Hotel, quieter than Yumoto.
good_for_us: Central for the loop through Gora and Lake Ashi
Classic hotels with Western beds
watch_out: Steep main street and station on a hillside
Few restaurants
Mountain train from Yumoto takes about 25 min, plus a change at Yumoto
areas.to_the_plans: Yumoto 25 min by train; Gora 10–15 min; Lake Ashi 25 min by bus.

areas.name: Gora
areas.what_its_like: The hub of the Hakone loop at the top of the mountain railway, with many upmarket ryokan with private open-air baths.
good_for_us: Open-Air Museum and the cable car to Owakudani start here
Lots of rooms with a private onsen bath
watch_out: Very steep streets around the station
45–60 min from Odawara, with crowded switchback trains
Further from the hospital
Owakudani's volcanic gas: pregnant women are advised not to go into the valley
areas.to_the_plans: Open-Air Museum 5–10 min; cable car at the station; Yumoto 35–40 min; Odawara 50–60 min.

areas.name: Sengokuhara
areas.what_its_like: A wide, flat highland valley with museums and resort hotels.
good_for_us: Flat walks around the hotels
Spacious resort rooms with beds
watch_out: No train: 30–40 min by bus from Yumoto, longer from Odawara
Really needs a car or taxis
Furthest from a hospital
areas.to_the_plans: Yumoto 30–40 min by bus; Lake Ashi (Togendai) 10–15 min by bus; Gora 15–20 min by bus.
areas.station: No station; Hakone-Yumoto is 30–40 min by bus

tips: Ask the ryokan for Western beds and an in-room bath. Hakone has many rooms with a private open-air bath, and they sell out early in January.
Pregnant women are advised not to enter the Owakudani valley because of volcanic gas. Fernanda could ride the ropeway over it, or skip it and do Lake Ashi.
Hakone's luggage service takes bags from Hakone-Yumoto station to partner inns in the morning, so you don't have to carry them up the mountain.

nara.why_pick: Kintetsu Nara station sits at the edge of Nara Park, so Kofuku-ji, the deer and Todai-ji are a flat 5–20 minute walk away, and the group can go back for a rest in the middle of the day. Kintetsu trains run straight into Kyoto Station in about 35 minutes for the 5 Jan shinkansen, and the station has lifts.

areas.name: Kintetsu Nara / Nara Park edge (Higashimuki, Noborioji)
areas.what_its_like: Small, walkable centre at the top of the covered Higashimuki shopping street, a few steps from the park.
good_for_us: Flat walk to Kofuku-ji (5–10 min) and Todai-ji (15–20 min)
Direct Kintetsu trains to Kyoto Station for leaving on 5 Jan
Covered shopping arcade for rainy days
watch_out: Very busy with New Year visitors on 3–5 Jan
Kasuga Taisha is a 25–30 min walk on gravel paths, gently uphill, so take a taxi there
areas.to_the_plans: Kofuku-ji 5–10 min; Todai-ji 15–20 min; Kasuga Taisha 25–30 min walk or 5–10 min by taxi; Kyoto Station about 35 min by Kintetsu limited express.

areas.name: Naramachi (old merchant quarter)
areas.what_its_like: Quiet lanes of old wooden houses just south of the park, with cafés and small guesthouses.
good_for_us: Lovely in the evening once the day crowds have gone
Whole-house rentals and small inns
watch_out: Old houses usually mean steep stairs and futons
10–15 min walk to Kintetsu Nara with bags
areas.to_the_plans: Kofuku-ji 10 min; Todai-ji 20–25 min; Kintetsu Nara 10–15 min; JR Nara 15–20 min.

areas.name: JR Nara Station area
areas.what_its_like: Flat, modern area of business hotels on the west side of the centre.
good_for_us: The JR Nara line runs Kyoto–Uji–Nara, so you can stop in Uji on the way in on 3 Jan
Bigger modern hotels with lifts
Usually cheaper

JR to Kyoto is slower than Kintetsu (45–75 min)
areas.to_the_plans: Kofuku-ji 15–20 min walk; Todai-ji 25–30 min or 10 min by bus; Uji 20–30 min by JR; Kyoto Station 45–75 min by JR.

tips: Book reserved seats on the Kintetsu limited express to Kyoto for 5 Jan, timed to connect with the shinkansen. Allow 15 min to change at Kyoto Station.
Ask for Western beds and a lift. Many central Nara inns are small and old. The bigger hotels near both stations are safer for Fernanda.
The nearest big hospital with a maternity centre is Nara Prefecture General Medical Center, about 15–20 min by taxi.
